articles.title: Shah Rukh Khan’s 'King' breaks overseas rights record at Rs 175 crore; eyes to top 'Pathaan', 'Jawan' collections to turn profitable
articles.summary: Even as big-budget South Indian films dominate the domestic market with their pan-India releases, Shah Rukh Khan continues to rule the overseas box office.
articles.body: Even as big-budget South Indian films dominate the domestic market with their pan-India releases, Shah Rukh Khan continues to rule the overseas box office. His upcoming film, 'King', is the latest proof. According to a new report, its overseas theatrical rights have been acquired for a staggering Rs 175 crore, setting a fresh record for Indian cinema. The deal highlights the actor’s unmatched global appeal and the enduring loyalty of his international fans.Phars Films pays record Rs 175 crore for Shah Rukh Khan’s ‘King’According to Pinkvilla, Phars Films has secured the overseas distribution rights for 'King' at Rs 175 crore, which is over $18 million. Until now, Yash Raj Films has handled the international release of Shah Rukh Khan’s films, successfully doing so for both 'Pathaan', produced under its own banner, and 'Jawan' in 2023. Phars, however, is no newcomer to the overseas market. It has worked alongside YRF on several titles and independently distributed Prabhas’ 'Saaho'. The report adds that Phars has paid a minimum guarantee of Rs 175 crore for the rights. Considering that no Indian film has crossed the Rs 100 crore mark overseas so far, the figure is truly staggering.What Shah Rukh Khan’s ‘King’ must earn to break evenThe minimum guarantee a distributor pays reflects the distributor's confidence in a film’s box-office run. Since overseas distributors typically keep just 50% of the gross, King would need to collect roughly $37-40 million, or about Rs 350-375 crore, internationally merely to break even. For perspective, Khan’s biggest hits, 'Pathaan' and 'Jawan', each brought in close to Rs 400 crore abroad, so 'King' must match that, or better it, to turn a profit. With such a steep guarantee, the film’s overseas earnings would need to rival those of 'Dhurandhar 2' (₹460 crore) or 'RRR' (Rs 430 crore), both among the biggest international successes Indian cinema has ever seen.Shah Rukh Khan’s ‘King’: Cast, director and release dateDirected by Siddharth Anand, 'King' has Shah Rukh Khan headlining the cast, reuniting the pair after their 2023 hit Pathaan. The ensemble also includes Deepika Padukone, Abhishek Bachchan, Rani Mukerji, Jaideep Ahlawat, Raghav Juyal and Saurabh Shukla. Notably, the film brings Shah Rukh together on screen with his daughter Suhana Khan for the first time, following her acting debut in The Archies in 2023. King is set to hit theatres on December 24.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Zaheer Iqbal says he and Sonakshi Sinha got several romantic film offers but picked 'Tu Hai Meri Kiran' for its shock value instead of repeating what 'we do on Instagram'
articles.summary: Zaheer Iqbal and his wife Sonakshi Sinha are loved for their playful chemistry and sweet social media moments.
articles.body: Zaheer Iqbal and his wife Sonakshi Sinha are loved for their playful chemistry and sweet social media moments. But the couple surprised fans by coming together for the thriller ‘Tu Hai Meri Kiran’, in which Zaheer plays a possessive lover. In a recent interview, the actor spoke about the film, his bond with Sonakshi and his Bollywood debut, which was backed by Salman Khan.Zaheer Iqbal on his role in ‘Tu Hai Meri Kiran’In a chat with Midday, Zaheer Iqbal said a lot of effort went into building his character. He shared, “We shot a lot. We shot extra stuff, and, on the edit, we had to remove certain things to simplify it or to make it less obvious sometimes. I did a lot of workshops, and I worked really hard on this character because it’s one opportunity that you get sometimes to do a character like this, and you don’t want to mess it up.”Choosing a different on-screen dynamicThe couple consciously chose not to play the cute and sweet pair that audiences know from their real life. Zaheer said, “If we did what we do off-screen or we do on Instagram, you’ll feel like you’re in a theatre scrolling on reels and you’ll want to be like swipe up.” He added that they had got many offers to play a romantic couple, but this film stood out for its shock value.In the film, their characters move from being engaged to being married. Zaheer explained, “So half the film, we were engaged and married for the other half.” He also praised Sonakshi, saying, “She is just so seasoned in what she does.”Is Zaheer Iqbal a possessive partner?On possessiveness in relationships, Zaheer feels it depends on the equation between two people and how secure they make each other feel. He said, “A lot of people are just inherently obsessive and possessive. But I think in a normal relationship like me and Sona, I feel it’s your partner who can make you possessive or not.”On the idea of equality, he said Sonakshi is superior. He explained, “I don’t believe men and women are equal. I believe women are way more superior because one can never be stronger than a woman who gave you birth.”On facing trollsZaheer Iqbal said the couple does not give much weight to online trolling. “I don’t see anything bad. I don’t feel we get trolled that much. And if we feel, we don’t pay attention,” he said.How Salman Khan gave him his first breakZaheer also recalled how he got into films after Salman Khan saw him dancing at his sister’s wedding. The offer came without warning, and he remains thankful for it. He said, “I was dancing somewhere at a wedding. My sister’s wedding, and Salman Khan happened to be there and offer me a film. So, it worked out that way. I got my chance. And it literally fell in my lap. And I don’t take that for granted ever. I don’t think there’s anybody else like that. In the industry right now, if you think there must be two or three people who were spotted like this. I’m glad I’m blessed.”Directed by Karan Rawal, 'Tu Hai Meri Kiran' was released in theatres on October 23, 2026.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Kajol, Sanjay Dutt, Raveena Tandon and others mourn filmmaker Sanjay Gupta's demise: 'Gone too soon'
articles.summary: Actors, including Kajol, Raveena Tandon and Sanjay Dutt, remembered \"full-of-life filmmaker\" Sanjay Gupta, whose credits include films such as \"Kaante\",
articles.body: Actors, including Kajol, Raveena Tandon and Sanjay Dutt, remembered "full-of-life filmmaker" Sanjay Gupta, whose credits include films such as "Kaante", "Shootout at Lokhandwala" and "Mumbai Saga", among others.Gupta died at his residence after he slipped and hit his head.Kajol shared a picture of the filmmaker on her Instagram handle on Saturday and said the news of Gupta's demise was "heartbreaking". "Sending love and immense strength to the family through this loss. Rest in peace," she wrote.Sanjay Dutt shared a series of pictures alongside the filmmaker with whom he has collaborated on films such as "Aatish: Feel the Fire" and "Kaante", among others."Gupts, my brother. I still cannot believe that you are gone. We have shared so much together, so many memories and so many years of friendship. You have always been family to me, and that will never change," he wrote.Dutt recalled his discussion about "Kante 2" with the filmmaker and said he will make the film in his memory."I will miss you, our conversations and all the times we spent together. We were just discussing 'Kante 2' recently, I will make 'Kaante 2' your dream, in memory of you my brother, I will do everything for this dream of yours to come true, love you forever and always. Life will not be the same without you, brother," he added.Tandon said, "Shocked to hear the shocking news of the untimely passing od dar Gups. Really saddened #sanjaygupta."Anupam Kher said Gupta was a "filmmaker with a distinctive style and an enormous love for cinema"."Woke up in Stockholm to the heartbreaking news of my friend and director Sanjay Gupta. You could ask him practically anything about movies, and a conversation with him would remind you how much he loved the world he belonged to. His passion came through in his social media posts too, where, of late, he had been expressing himself so openly. I worked with him in two films. But he also holds a special place in our family's journey. He was Sikandar's first director," he wrote.Kher said he was an "encyclopedia of films". "Kher saab, we must work together!"That was almost always his opening line whenever we met. He said it when I last met him, about a year ago. We always think there will be time. Another meeting. Another conversation. Another film. It hurts to know that this one will remain unfinished.I remember his warmth, his affection, and a lovely Holi party at his home few years back," he added.Hansal Mehta shared a picture alongside Gupta on his Instagram handle along with a note and said they went through many lows and highs together. "Not done, bro. Sanjay Gupta. Gups. My only boss in the film industry, perhaps. But more than that, a dear friend. We went through many lows and many highs together, and through all of it we shared a love for the good things in life," he wrote."My first and only Rolex came from him. Today it's the one memory of him I carry on my wrist, and I don't think I'll ever take it off. He held my hand when I was at my lowest. We didn't exactly create magic together, but the time itself was an absolute blast..."I watched some of the best films of my life in his theatre. I borrowed some of the best books I've read from his shelves. My bro code began with you, Sanjay. And now it is ended," he added.Kunal Kohli said, "Don't know how to process this news. #SanjayGupta RIP. Chatted with him little over a month ago. We were both on an awards show jury couple of years ago - we were equally quick to have an argument & a laugh about it later. You had many more films and many years to go. Prayers and strength to the family," in the post.Dia Mirza, who has worked with Gupta on "Dus Kahaniyaan", shared a picture of the filmmaker on her Instagram story and said she is grateful for their collaboration."Sanjay Gupta, I will always be grateful for the work we did together, the love, the respect and the support I got from you. RIP Gupta Saab. Deepest condolences to the family," she wrote.Neil Nitin Mukesh said he is "deeply saddened and shocked" by the death of Gupta. "A powerhouse filmmaker we all loved and respected. Gone far too soon. My heartfelt condolences to his family and loved ones."Tusshar Kapoor uploaded a note on his X handle and said "Woke up to sad news about the unfortunate and sudden demise of my beloved director @_SanjayGupta," he wrote."Life is so unpredictable, though this man was a lesson learned in living life to the fullest! My deepest condolences to his family, RIP sir," he added."Deeply saddened by this tragic news. May his soul rest in eternal peace," Madhur Bhandarkar said.Kangana Ranaut shared a picture of the actor on her Instagram story as she remembered him. "Sanjay Gupta jis demise has sent shock waves across the film industry, extremely sad and horrific news, have worked with him closely and what is unsettling is that he was not even unwell, terrible," she said.Lyricist and poet Manoj Muntashir recalled his collaboration with the director. "We only worked together in two films, one of which was-'Kaabil'. In the time we spent together, I learned that Sanjay was not just an outstanding filmmaker, but also an incredible friend," he wrote.Navjot Gulati said Gupta was among the most "funny and full-of-life filmmakers". "It is unbelievable that @_SanjayGupta is no more with us," he wrote."Other than being a filmmaker who made many COOL movies, his insights on life and the business of movies were a thing of beauty. And a true blue cinephile. RIP Sir. Oopar Kisi Screening room mein milege," he added.Gupta is known for making action-thriller and crime films such as "Aatish", "Kaabil", "Shootout at Lokhandwala", "Shootout at Wadala", "Jazbaa", "Zinda", and "Mumbai Saga", among others.He is survived by his wife, Anuradha Lekhi Gupta, and their children, Shivaansh Gupta and Dalai Gupta.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Sanjay Gupta passes away: Fardeen Khan, Ronit Roy, Rakesh Roshan and others pay last respects at filmmaker's Mumbai residence
articles.summary: Following the news of filmmaker Sanjay Gupta's demise on Saturday morning, several friends and members of the film fraternity gathered at his Mumbai
articles.body: Following the news of filmmaker Sanjay Gupta's demise on Saturday morning, several friends and members of the film fraternity gathered at his Mumbai residence to pay their last respects.Among those spotted arriving at the filmmaker's residence were actors Fardeen Khan, Ronit Roy, Rohit Roy and Gulshan Grover, filmmaker Rakesh Roshan, director Milap Zaveri, actor Sudhanshu Pandey and filmmaker Ashoke Pandit, among others.Ronit Roy and Milap Zaveri appeared visibly emotional, with tears in their eyes as they mourned the filmmaker’s demise.Sanjay Gupta, best known for directing films such as 'Kaante' and 'Shootout at Lokhandwala', passed away at the age of 57.As per Mumbai Police, Producer Sanjay Gupta, residing within the jurisdiction of the Versova Police Station, passed away late last night. He reportedly lost his balance and fell inside his home, sustaining a head injury that led to bleeding and, ultimately, his death. He lived in the bungalow with his wife, two children, and a domestic help; however, as everyone was asleep at the time, the incident was only discovered this morning. The family has expressed no suspicions or complaints. The body has been sent for a post-mortem examination.According to Mumbai Police, Sanjay Gupta, who resided within the jurisdiction of Versova Police Station, passed away late on Friday night after reportedly losing his balance and falling inside his residence. He sustained a head injury that resulted in bleeding and ultimately led to his death.As per the police, Gupta was living in the bungalow with his wife, two children and a domestic help. However, since everyone was asleep at the time of the incident, it was discovered only on Saturday morning.The family has reportedly expressed no suspicion or raised any complaint regarding the circumstances surrounding his death. His body has been sent for a post-mortem examination.Further details regarding his funeral are awaited.On the professional front, his last directorial venture was The Miranda Brothers, starring Harshvardhan Rane and Meezaan Jafri, which was released in 2024. As a producer, he also came up with 'Visfot', featuring Fardeen Khan and Riteish Deshmukh. Before that, he directed Mumbai Saga (2021), starring John Abraham and Emraan Hashmi in lead roles.However, Gupta was widely recognised for directing crime dramas such as 'Shootout at Lokhandwala' and 'Kaante', which established his presence in the crime thriller genre.His other directorial ventures included 'Kaabil' and 'Shootout at Wadala'.Known for his work in action and crime-based films, Gupta made a significant contribution to Hindi cinema through his distinctive storytelling and films centred on crime, action and drama.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Young artists turn to handmade forms to explore memory, identity and ecology
articles.summary: Ten emerging artists working with materials ranging from clay and glass to textiles, natural dyes, wood and reclaimed rubber are part of Insubordinate
articles.body: Ten emerging artists working with materials ranging from clay and glass to textiles, natural dyes, wood and reclaimed rubber are part of Insubordinate Matter, the sixth edition of Emami Art’s annual IMAGINARIUM open-call exhibition. On display at Gallery 2 and 3 of Emami Art until December 26, the exhibition brings together practices that explore the relationship between material, memory, the body and the natural environment.Launched in 2020, IMAGINARIUM was conceived to support young and emerging visual artists through awards, exhibitions and mentorship. This year, the open call received more than 1,200 portfolios, which were reviewed by a jury comprising artist Ibrahim Mahama, May Makki, Siddharth Somaiya, Shaunak Mahbubani and Emami Art director and head curator Ushmita Sahu. Ten artists were selected for the exhibition, with three receiving the annual awards.Bhagyashri Dange received the first award of Rs 2 lakh, followed by Sonu Pujar, who received the second award of Rs 1.5 lakh, and Subhash Deka, who received the third award of Rs 1 lakh. The awards are supported by the Emami Foundation and Kolkata Centre for Creativity.The exhibition takes the position that material is not merely a medium for artistic expression but can also hold memory and carry meaning. The works examine two broad concerns: the body and its inherited histories, and the natural world under pressure. Through handmade and often tactile forms, the artists explore questions of identity, gender, ecology, labour and collective memory.“The strength of this year’s cohort lies in its materiality. These are artists who think through substance, through clay and glass, cloth, wood and reclaimed matter, and who treat the made object not as a surface for ideas but as something living, that holds memory and carries a fragile world,” said Sahu.The participating artists approach these concerns through varied practices. Dange works across drawing, painting and printmaking to examine the body as a site of memory and conditioning, while Pujar uses textiles, organic matter and domestic materials to explore gendered labour, care and personal histories. Deka draws on natural rhythms and environmental phenomena to create sculptural works reflecting the relationship between people and their surroundings.Other artists bring distinct material approaches to the exhibition. Srijita Raha works with textiles and natural dyes to explore girlhood, vulnerability and psychological space. Annanya Dhanda draws on domestic objects and familial histories, particularly mother-daughter relationships, while Ayushi Shukla engages with traditional visual languages and the cultural memory of the Ganga.The remaining participants are Tithi Das, whose paintings draw on archival photographs and emotional inheritance; Dibbya Mudi, who transforms discarded industrial rubber through weaving and stitching; Shibayan Halder, whose multidisciplinary practice examines environmental change and the relationship between people and place; and Siya Raju, who works with ceramics and glass to explore natural forms and human relationships.Speaking about the initiative, Richa Agarwal, founder-director of Emami Art, said the open call was established to address the gap between artistic talent and the opportunities available to young practitioners. “What matters to us is not recognition alone, but giving emerging artists the standing and the support a young practice needs at the moment it is most fragile,” she said.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Sasi clarifies why 'Nooru Kodi Vaanavil' skipped theatrical release; Harish Kalyan says, 'film is like child'
articles.summary: Director Sasi's romantic drama 'Nooru Kodi Vaanavil', starring Harish Kalyan and Siddhi Idnani, is finally set to reach audiences after a long wait for
articles.body: Director Sasi's romantic drama 'Nooru Kodi Vaanavil', starring Harish Kalyan and Siddhi Idnani, is finally set to reach audiences after a long wait for its theatrical release. The film will now premiere directly on OTT. The film, which explores love, family relationships, and difficult life choices, is now set to premiere directly on OTT. The makers have announced that the film will stream on ZEE5 from November 6 as a special Diwali release.Sasi clarifies why 'Nooru Kodi Vaanavil' did not release in theatresDuring a recent interaction with Behindwoods, both Sasi and Harish Kalyan were asked why the film was not released in theatres despite its promising trailer. Responding to the question, director Sasi clarified that the decision had nothing to do with the creative aspects of the film. He said, "For some reasons, which we could not say or avoid, there was no creative side to it. From the production side, they felt that bringing the film directly to OTT would give us better results. So, we were happy that the film was released." His statement made it clear that the decision was taken entirely by the production team.Harish Kalyan says it was painful to wait for the film's releaseHarish Kalyan also shared his feelings about the film finally reaching viewers, although it missed a theatrical release. Comparing a film to a child, the actor explained how difficult it was to wait for it to reach audiences. He said, "A film is like a child. There is a pain when it does not reach anyone. That is very difficult. But we do not have the mindset that the film must only reach audiences in theatres. It has reached an OTT platform, and many people are watching it. So, we are happy that our product has finally been released." Sasi, however, described his feelings as relief rather than happiness, adding, "We cannot say we are happy. We can say it is a relief. What you say about the film after watching it will make us happy."'Nooru Kodi Vaanavil' cast and delayed production journey'Nooru Kodi Vaanavil' also features Kovai Sarala, Thambi Ramaiah, Chinni Jayanth and Sampath Raj in important roles. The project faced production delays due to the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly during the second wave, when the team could not travel to Mumbai for a planned schedule. Sasi revealed that portions were shot in Goa, while the Mumbai schedule remained pending, adding to the delay. Now, after a long wait, the director's romantic drama is finally ready to meet viewers through OTT.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more.
